description: Saved Sol analysis whose PF realization plate for oku -DIK-AGR.3SG -(n)I (stage 4) was placed below the tree, far from its owner. Test input for tests/realizationPlateNearOwner.test.mjs.
sentence: Ahmet'in dün kütüphaneden aldığı kitabı Ayşe'nin çoktan okuduğunu biliyorum.

derivationStages.statement: Construct the relative clause with its object operator in the thematic position.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The relative predicate al ‘take/obtain’ is merged with a silent nominal operator as its Theme, and Ahmet'in occupies the subject position as Agent. The predicate licenses abstract accusative on its object operator. Nominal participial inflection licenses genitive on Ahmet'in and agrees with that third-person singular subject. The ablative nominal kütüphaneden modifies the event as its Source, while dün locates that same taking event yesterday. The relative complementizer is silent. This analysis uses classical subject-in-Spec-IP phrase structure; nominal case on ordinary nouns is represented in their lexical forms, while the verbal participial ending is represented separately in I.

derivationStages.statement: Complete the relative dependency and attach the relative clause to kitabı.
derivationStages.stageRecord: First, al raises to the participial I, leaving a verbal trace; the resulting head complex is realized as aldığı. Next, the silent object operator moves from the complement of al to Spec-CP, leaving an accusative object trace. The Theme and abstract accusative dependencies now terminate at that trace, and the operator binds it as an A-bar chain. The noun kitabı is then introduced, and its nominal projection is modified by the relative CP. Identification of the head noun with the operator restricts the book referent to what Ahmet obtained from the library yesterday. The accusative form kitabı is present lexically but awaits a selecting predicate that licenses its structural case.

values.interpretation: the book is the Theme of Ahmet's taking
the book that Ahmet obtained from the library yesterday

derivationStages.statement: Build the nominalized embedded clause with the book in its base object position.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The complete book NP is merged as the complement of oku ‘read’, which assigns it the Theme role and licenses its accusative case. Ayşe'nin is merged as the embedded Agent in Spec-IP. Nominal inflection licenses genitive on Ayşe'nin and agrees with that third-person singular subject. Çoktan modifies the reading event, contributing ‘already/by then’. The embedded clause is nominalized rather than finite. In this implementation its C edge bears the accusative suffix of the nominalized clause; this clausal case remains to be licensed by the matrix verb. The book is still after the embedded subject at this stage, so its eventual preverbal-clausal position has not been stipulated as a base position.

values.interpretation: Ayşe has already read the book

derivationStages.statement: Form the embedded verbal inflectional complex okuduğunu.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Oku raises from V to embedded I, leaving a silent verbal trace. Its combination with nominal -DIK and third-person singular agreement, together with the clause-edge accusative ending, receives the collective realization okuduğunu. The case ending is thus pronounced with the nominalized predicate even though its syntactic bearer is the nominal clause. No nominal argument moves in this stage.

derivationStages.statement: Scramble the embedded object to the left of Ayşe'nin.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The entire accusative book NP, including its relative clause, moves from the complement position of oku to a left-adjoined IP position within the nominalized embedded clause. This local A-bar scrambling derives the observed order in which kitabı precedes Ayşe'nin without making the book an argument of biliyorum. The movement leaves an object trace governed by the reading predicate. The Theme and accusative dependencies now terminate at that trace and are transmitted through the scrambling chain to the pronounced NP. The moved relative clause remains intact, including its separate operator dependency.

values.movement: local object scrambling to IP adjunction

derivationStages.statement: Embed the nominalized proposition under bil and license the silent matrix subject.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Bil ‘know’ selects the complete nominalized embedded CP as its propositional complement and assigns it the propositional Theme role; the matrix subject pro receives the Experiencer role. The matrix verb licenses accusative on the nominalized CP, whose case exponent is the ending already represented at the embedded C edge. Finite matrix I licenses nominative on pro. Its first-person singular agreement identifies this silent subject as the speaker, so neither Ahmet nor Ayşe is the matrix subject. The matrix inflection is present progressive in form, yielding the ordinary current-state interpretation ‘I know’ with this stative verb.

derivationStages.statement: Complete the matrix inflection and the surface derivation.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Bil raises to finite I and leaves a verbal trace. The resulting combination of bil, present-progressive inflection, and first-person singular agreement is realized as biliyorum. The completed structure therefore says that the speaker knows that Ayşe has already read the book that Ahmet obtained from the library yesterday. Its surface order follows from head-final projections, relative-operator movement, and local scrambling of the embedded book object; the matrix subject and all movement traces remain silent.
